findings.title: Laravel 8 no longer receives security fixes
findings.explanation: Vulnerabilities discovered in this Laravel version will not be patched upstream. This is a maintenance risk, not proof of a current vulnerability.
findings.remediation: Plan an upgrade to a supported Laravel release. Upgrade one major version at a time, following the official upgrade guides.

findings.title: guzzlehttp/guzzle 7.5.0 has 9 known security advisories
findings.explanation: The locked version falls within the affected range of published advisories. Whether the application is exploitable depends on how the package is used.
findings.evidence:
- CVE-2026-69246 (high): Guzzle: Noncanonical host can bypass host-based checks; affected >=8.0.0,<8.0.1|<7.15.2 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-v5mv-p594-2x33)
- CVE-2026-69245 (medium): Guzzle: Noncanonical cookie domain keeps subdomain scope; affected >=8.0.0,<8.0.1|<7.15.2 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-f7vp-7xgx-4w4r)
- CVE-2026-67354 (medium): Guzzle: URI fragments disclosed in redirect Referer headers; affected <7.15.1 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-h95v-h523-3mw8)
- CVE-2026-67355 (medium): Guzzle: Host-only cookie scope is not preserved; affected <7.15.1 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wm3w-8rrp-j577)
- CVE-2026-67353 (medium): Guzzle: Unbounded response cookies risk denial of service; affected <7.15.1 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-f283-ghqc-fg79)
- CVE-2026-59883 (medium): Guzzle: Cookie Disclosure and Injection via IP-Address Domains; affected <7.12.3 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g446-98w2-8p5w)
- CVE-2026-67339 (medium): Guzzle: Proxy-Authorization headers can be sent to origin servers; affected <7.14.2 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-94pj-82f3-465w)
- CVE-2026-55767 (medium): Dot-only cookie domains match all hosts; affected <7.12.1 (https://github.com/guzzle/guzzle/security/advisories/GHSA-cwxw-98qj-8qjx)
- CVE-2026-55568 (medium): Silent HTTPS proxy downgrade to cleartext; affected <7.12.1 (https://github.com/guzzle/guzzle/security/advisories/GHSA-wpwq-4j6v-78m3)
findings.remediation: Update guzzlehttp/guzzle to a version outside the affected ranges (>=8.0.0,<8.0.1|<7.15.2; <7.15.1; <7.12.3; <7.14.2; <7.12.1), e.g. "composer update guzzlehttp/guzzle" in the project, then run the test suite.

findings.title: 5 direct dependencies are behind a major release
findings.explanation: Newer major versions exist. Staying far behind makes future upgrades and security patches harder. Major updates may include breaking changes.
findings.evidence:
- fruitcake/laravel-cors v2.2.0 -> v3.0.0
- guzzlehttp/guzzle 7.5.0 -> 8.3.1
- laravel/framework v8.83.27 -> v13.39.0
- laravel/sanctum v2.15.1 -> v4.3.3
- phpunit/phpunit 9.5.28 -> 12.5.42
findings.remediation: Review the changelogs and upgrade guides, then update one package at a time.

notes: Routes were read from source without booting the application. Routes registered by packages (e.g. Telescope, Horizon, Filament, Sanctum) and routes built dynamically are not included; use --use-artisan to list them.
Installed packages that register their own routes (not listed above): Sanctum.

findings.title: Log level is "debug" in production
findings.explanation: Debug-level logging in production produces large logs and is more likely to record request data, queries or tokens.
findings.remediation: Set LOG_LEVEL to "info", "warning" or "error" in the production environment.

results.title: Database

findings.title: Models exist but there are no migrations
findings.explanation: The schema cannot be recreated from the repository, which makes testing and new environments harder. The schema may be managed elsewhere (a dump file, another repository).
findings.evidence: app/Models contains classes; database/migrations has no PHP files.
findings.remediation: Add migrations (or a schema dump via "php artisan schema:dump") so the schema is versioned with the code.

notes: The database was not connected to. Schema details come from migration files only; tables created by packages or by raw SQL may be missing.

results.title: Security

tables.title: Security checks with findings
rows: Debug mode is enabled in a production environment

findings.title: Debug mode is enabled in a production environment
findings.explanation: With APP_DEBUG=true, error pages show stack traces, configuration values and environment variables, including credentials, to anyone who triggers an error. Older debug page versions have also had remote code execution vulnerabilities.
findings.remediation: Set APP_DEBUG=false in the production environment and run "php artisan config:cache" after deploying.

findings.title: .env is world-readable
findings.explanation: Any local user or process on the server can read the application's credentials.
findings.remediation: Restrict it to the owner and the web server group, e.g. chmod 640 .env.

notes: Git tracking could not be determined (not a git checkout, git unavailable, or the repository is not trusted by git), so "committed file" checks were skipped.
tests/ is not scanned. Code findings are pattern-based and local to single expressions; they need manual review and do not prove exploitability.

results.title: Architecture

facts.label: Overview
facts.value: Laravel 8 application using the classic kernel-based structure with 6 controllers, 1 model and 11 routes. It is primarily a server-rendered web application. Business logic appears to live in controllers and models (no service, action or repository layer detected).
facts.origin: derived from detected classes, packages and routes

facts.label: Frontend
facts.value: No server-rendered views or SPA bridge detected

notes: This overview is inferred from file structure, class inheritance and installed packages. A missing conventional directory does not mean anything is wrong.

data.overview: Laravel 8 application using the classic kernel-based structure with 6 controllers, 1 model and 11 routes. It is primarily a server-rendered web application. Business logic appears to live in controllers and models (no service, action or repository layer detected).

results.title: Code Quality

findings.title: No automated tests found
findings.explanation: Without tests, upgrades (including security updates of Laravel and dependencies) cannot be verified quickly, so they tend to be postponed.
findings.evidence: No *Test.php files under tests/ (PHPUnit is installed).
findings.remediation: Start with feature tests for the most important routes (php artisan make:test), and run them in CI.

findings.title: No static analysis tool is installed
findings.explanation: Static analysis finds type errors and dead code before they reach production, and makes refactoring safer.
findings.evidence: None of phpstan/phpstan, larastan/larastan or vimeo/psalm is required.
findings.remediation: Add Larastan: composer require --dev larastan/larastan, then start at a low level and raise it over time.

findings.title: No code style tool is installed
findings.explanation: A formatter keeps diffs focused on behaviour and avoids style discussions in reviews.
findings.evidence: None of laravel/pint, friendsofphp/php-cs-fixer or squizlabs/php_codesniffer is required.
findings.remediation: Add Laravel Pint (composer require --dev laravel/pint) and run it in CI with --test.

findings.title: No continuous integration configuration found
findings.explanation: Without CI, tests and checks depend on each developer remembering to run them. CI may be configured outside the repository (e.g. in a hosting platform).
findings.remediation: Add a pipeline that runs composer install, the test suite, static analysis, the formatter in check mode and composer audit.

notes: Tools were detected but not run. Use --run-quality-tools (or --run-quality-tools=phpstan,pint) to run them; you will be asked to confirm.
